why: Designing the state for two sequences: ways[j] = number of ways the first j pattern characters appear as a subsequence of the text read so far. Each text character can extend every slot where it matches.
hints: Brute force over triples of positions is O(n^3). Read s2 once and remember partial matches instead.
Keep ways[0..3]: ways[0] = 1, ways[j] = number of ways to have matched s1[:j]. A character equal to s1[j-1] adds ways[j-1] to ways[j].
Update j from high to low for each character so one character does not fill two slots at once. Answer ways[3]. O(|s2| * |s1|).
pitfalls: Updating j upward lets one character play two roles when s1 has repeated letters (e.g. 'AAB').
The count can be about 10^16 for |s2| = 5*10^5, so it needs 64-bit integers.
